data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: accommodation
sections.summary: A place where someone lives or stays, especially temporarily; the rooms, buildings or other spaces provided for someone to sleep and live in.

senses.definition: a place where someone stays or lives temporarily, such as a hotel, hostel or rented flat
examples: We booked our accommodation online several weeks before flying out to the island.

senses.definition: a convenient arrangement or compromise reached between two people or groups
examples: After lengthy discussions, the two sides finally reached an accommodation that both found acceptable.

answers.answer: The travel package includes return flights, accommodation and a guided city tour.
She showed great accommodation in solving the navigation problem the tour guide had presented.
He put the accommodation carefully into his suitcase before leaving for the airport.
The accommodation arrived exactly on time at the station and took them to the hotel.

sections.question: itinerary
sections.summary: A detailed plan or route for a journey, listing the places to be visited, activities to be done and times of travel.

senses.definition: a detailed plan of a journey, showing the route, places to visit and times of travel or events
examples: The travel agent sent us a detailed itinerary covering every day of our two-week trip.

answers.answer: She printed out the itinerary and shared it with everyone in the travel group.
He wore his best itinerary to the farewell dinner on the last night of the cruise.
She ate the itinerary quickly and then went back to the hotel to rest before the evening tour.
The itinerary was very comfortable and easy to carry around the city on a warm afternoon.

sections.question: landmark
sections.summary: A well-known and easily recognisable building, structure or feature in a landscape; also an important event or development.

senses.definition: a building, structure or place that is easily recognised and often considered an important part of a place's identity
examples: The Eiffel Tower is one of the most recognisable landmarks in the entire world.

senses.definition: an important event or development that marks a major change or stage
examples: The discovery of penicillin was a landmark in the history of modern medicine.

answers.answer: The ancient cathedral is the most visited landmark in the entire region.
She felt a great landmark when she finally arrived at the destination after twelve hours of travel.
He bought a landmark from the local market to take home as a gift for his family.
The landmark was very delicious and the tourists enjoyed it at the hotel restaurant each evening.

sections.question: reservation
sections.summary: An arrangement to have something kept for you, such as a table at a restaurant, a room in a hotel or a seat on a flight; also a feeling of doubt or hesitation.

senses.definition: an arrangement to have a place, room, table or seat kept for you in advance
examples: She made a reservation at the restaurant two weeks in advance to guarantee a table by the window.

senses.definition: a feeling of doubt or uncertainty about something
examples: He agreed to the proposal but had some reservations about the timeline.

answers.answer: She called ahead to make a reservation for four people at the hotel restaurant.
The reservation was very comfortable and had a spectacular view of the surrounding mountains.
He showed great reservation in packing his suitcase the night before the early morning flight.
She felt reservation in her stomach as the plane began to descend towards the destination.

sections.question: sightseeing
sections.summary: The activity of visiting and looking at interesting or famous places, especially as a tourist.

senses.definition: the activity of visiting famous or interesting places as a tourist
examples: They spent the whole morning sightseeing and visited three museums before stopping for lunch.

answers.answer: After checking in at the hotel, the group went sightseeing around the old town for the afternoon.
She bought some sightseeing from the gift shop at the airport to send to friends back home.
He showed great sightseeing in navigating the unfamiliar city streets with only a paper map.
She put her sightseeing into her bag and took it to the tourist information centre.

sections.question: tourist attraction
sections.summary: A place, building or event that is popular with tourists because of its beauty, historical significance or entertainment value.

senses.definition: a place or thing that many people visit because it is interesting, beautiful or historically important
examples: The ancient ruins have become one of the country's most visited tourist attractions.

answers.answer: The city's harbour is its most famous tourist attraction, drawing millions of visitors each year.
He showed great tourist attraction when speaking to the local people in their own language.
She wrote a tourist attraction in her notebook to remember everything she had seen that day.
He carried a tourist attraction in his bag to read on the long flight back home.

sections.question: travel agency
sections.summary: A company or shop that makes travel arrangements for people, such as booking flights, hotels and holiday packages.

senses.definition: a business that arranges travel, accommodation and holidays for customers
examples: She booked the entire holiday through a travel agency rather than organising it herself online.

answers.answer: They visited a travel agency to get advice on the best routes and hotels for their trip.
He went to the travel agency to buy some sunscreen, a hat and a pair of sunglasses.
The travel agency was very relaxing and everyone felt calm and refreshed after their visit.
She showed great travel agency in planning the group trip and booking everything on time.

sections.question: traveler
sections.summary: A person who is travelling or who travels frequently, especially to different countries or places; UK spelling: traveller.

senses.definition: a person who is on a journey or who travels frequently, especially to other countries
examples: The experienced traveler always keeps a digital copy of her passport in case of emergencies.

senses.definition: a person who moves from place to place and does not have a permanent home
examples: The campsite was traditionally used by travelers passing through the region in summer.

answers.answer: As an experienced traveler, she always arrived at the airport two hours before departure.
She bought a traveler from the airport bookshop to read on the long flight to New Zealand.
He showed great traveler in finding the fastest route through the unfamiliar city streets.
The traveler was very tasty and the tourists enjoyed it at the hotel buffet each morning.

sections.question: vacation
sections.summary: A period of time away from work or school, spent resting or travelling for pleasure; used mainly in American English (British English: holiday).

senses.definition: a period of time when you stop work or school and travel or rest for pleasure (mainly used in American English; British English: holiday)
examples: The family spent their summer vacation exploring the mountains of northern Portugal.

senses.definition: one of the fixed periods of the year when universities and law courts are officially closed
examples: She used the long summer vacation to complete her research and write her first paper.

answers.answer: They decided to spend their vacation travelling along the coast by bicycle and staying in small guesthouses.
She showed great vacation in completing all her work reports before the long weekend.
He put the vacation in his bag and took it to the office to show to his manager.
The vacation was so heavy that it took two people to carry it to the hotel room.

sections.question: visa
sections.summary: An official stamp or document placed in a passport allowing the holder to enter, stay in or leave a particular country.

senses.definition: an official document or stamp in a passport giving permission to enter, stay in or leave a particular country
examples: She applied for a tourist visa three months before her planned trip to the United States.

answers.answer: He was stopped at the border because he did not have the correct visa to enter the country.
She used her visa to pay for the hotel room and the taxi from the airport on arrival.
He showed the visa to the waiter and was immediately given the best table in the restaurant.
The visa was very comfortable and offered a spectacular view of the sea from every room.
